How it works

Choose a sentence and press the microphone to record up to 30 seconds, or choose Live and say anything. Live transcribes your own words and keeps listening until you stop it. Use the upload icon to select a portion of an audio file.

Pitch

Letters follow the rise and fall of your voice. Playback begins with straight lettering, then reveals the movement as you speak. Tap any word to replay it.

Rhythm & emphasis

Longer sounds make letters wider and taller. Coral segments follow measured energy within each word; their thickness estimates prominence.

Pauses

Dashed connections span quiet intervals. Short unvoiced sounds are connected smoothly.

About the analysis

Pitch is measured from your audio with YIN. The display follows voiced pitch at 20 ms intervals and interpolates between measurements, so a continuous line does not mean pitch exists through silence. Word timing uses English speech models; timing and emphasis are estimates. After Live stops, acoustic alignment refines replay word and character timing. Low-confidence boundaries remain estimates. Whispers may have no measurable pitch; a neutral dashed baseline then shows timing and energy. Layout expands for readability.

Live pitch, energy and pauses respond from small audio windows. Your own words appear as the on-device English model catches up; partial words can change as more speech arrives. New words fill each line from left to right. Earlier lines move upward inside the card. Scroll up to review the whole session; your place stays fixed while speech continues. Use the down arrow to follow the latest speech. Session text and contours remain until you clear or reload. Listening continues until you stop; up to 30 seconds ending with your latest speech stay available for replay. Live uses Whisper for English dictation (about 79 MB on first use); the replay timing and sample/upload model is about 95 MB. Models load in the background while recording remains available. Uploaded selections use the words actually spoken. Audio stays in your browser.

Thin letterforms are adapted from The Straits Times’ interactive, with matching monoline forms for additional characters.
